questions.stem: Consider the points $\text{A}(-2,\ 20)$, $\text{B}(4,\ 6)$ and $\text{C}(-14,\ 12)$. The line $L$ passes through the point $\text{A}$ and is perpendicular to $[\text{BC}]$.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
$m_{\text{BC}} = \dfrac{12 - 6}{-14 - 4} \left(= -\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$ ***(A1)***

finding $m_L = \dfrac{-1}{m_{\text{BC}}}$ using their $m_{\text{BC}}$ ***(M1)***

$m_L = 3$

$y - 20 = 3(x + 2)$, $\ y = 3x + 26$ ***A1***

> **Note:** Do not accept $L = 3x + 26$.

parts.label: b
parts.intro: The line $L$ passes through the point $(k,\ 2)$.

questions.stem:
A survey at a swimming pool is given to one adult in each family. The age of the adult, $a$ years old, and of their eldest child, $c$ years old, are recorded.

The ages of the eldest child are summarized in the following box and whisker diagram.

![Box and whisker diagram of the ages of the eldest child (years): minimum 2, lower quartile 6, median 7, upper quartile 10, maximum 18. Diagram not to scale.](content/papers/img/2022-may-p1-tz1-q3.png)

**diagram not to scale**

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the largest value of $c$ that would not be considered an outlier.

parts.label: b
parts.intro: The regression line of $a$ on $c$ is $a = \dfrac{7}{4}c + 20$. The regression line of $c$ on $a$ is $c = \dfrac{1}{2}a - 9$.
parts.text:
(i) One of the adults surveyed is 42 years old. Estimate the age of their eldest child.

(ii) Find the mean age of all the adults surveyed.
parts.markscheme:
(i) choosing $c = \dfrac{1}{2}a - 9$ ***(M1)***

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times 42 - 9$

$= 12$ (years old) ***A1***

(ii) attempt to solve system by substitution or elimination ***(M1)***

$34$ (years old) ***A1***

questions.stem: Consider the functions $f(x) = \sqrt{3}\sin x + \cos x$ where $0 \leq x \leq \pi$ and $g(x) = 2x$ where $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the equation $(f \circ g)(x) = 2\cos 2x$ where $0 \leq x \leq \pi$.
parts.markscheme:
$\sqrt{3}\sin 2x + \cos 2x = 2\cos 2x$

$\sqrt{3}\sin 2x = \cos 2x$

recognising to use $\tan$ or $\cot$ ***M1***

$\tan 2x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ OR $\cot 2x = \sqrt{3}$ (values may be seen in right triangle) ***(A1)***

$\left(\arctan\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \right) \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ (seen anywhere) (accept degrees) ***(A1)***

$2x = \dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$

$x = \dfrac{\pi}{12},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{12}$ ***A1A1***

> **Note:** Do not award the final ***A1*** if any additional solutions are seen.  
> Award ***A1A0*** for correct answers in degrees.  
> Award ***A0A0*** for correct answers in degrees with additional values.

questions.stem:
Consider $f(x) = 4\sin x + 2.5$ and $g(x) = 4\sin\left(x - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) + 2.5 + q$, where $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $q > 0$.

The graph of $g$ is obtained by two transformations of the graph of $f$.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
translation (shift) by $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ to the right/positive horizontal direction ***A1***

translation (shift) by $q$ upwards/positive vertical direction ***A1***

> **Note:** accept translation by $\begin{pmatrix} \dfrac{3\pi}{2} \\[4pt] q \end{pmatrix}$  
> **Do not accept** ‘move’ for translation/shift.

parts.label: b
parts.intro: The $y$-intercept of the graph of $g$ is at $(0,\ r)$.
parts.text: Given that $g(x) \geq 7$, find the smallest value of $r$.
parts.markscheme:
**METHOD 1**

minimum of $4\sin\left(x - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ is $-4$ (may be seen in sketch) ***(M1)***

$-4 + 2.5 + q \geq 7$

$q \geq 8.5$ (accept $q = 8.5$) ***A1***

substituting $x = 0$ and their $q \ (= 8.5)$ to find $r$ ***(M1)***

$(r =)\ 4\sin\left(\dfrac{-3\pi}{2}\right) + 2.5 + 8.5$

$4 + 2.5 + 8.5$ ***(A1)***

smallest value of $r$ is $15$ ***A1***

**METHOD 2**

substituting $x = 0$ to find an expression (for $r$) in terms of $q$ ***(M1)***

$(g(0) = r =)\ 4\sin\left(\dfrac{-3\pi}{2}\right) + 2.5 + q$

$(r =)\ 6.5 + q$ ***A1***

minimum of $4\sin\left(x - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ is $-4$ ***(M1)***

$-4 + 2.5 + q \geq 7$

$-4 + 2.5 + (r - 6.5) \geq 7$ (accept $=$) ***(A1)***

smallest value of $r$ is $15$ ***A1***

**METHOD 3**

$4\sin\left(x - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) + 2.5 + q = 4\cos x + 2.5 + q$ ***A1***

$y$-intercept of $4\cos x + 2.5 + q$ is a maximum ***(M1)***

amplitude of $g(x)$ is $4$ ***(A1)***

attempt to find least maximum ***(M1)***

$r = 2 \times 4 + 7$

smallest value of $r$ is $15$ ***A1***

questions.stem:
A function, $f$, has its derivative given by $f'(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + p$, where $p \in \mathbb{R}$. The following diagram shows part of the graph of $f'$.

![Graph of f′: an upward parabola that crosses the y-axis above the origin and touches the x-axis at its vertex, to the right of the y-axis.](content/papers/img/2022-may-p1-tz1-q7.png)

The graph of $f'$ has an axis of symmetry $x = q$.

parts.label: a
parts.markscheme:
**EITHER**

attempt to use $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$ ***(M1)***

$q = -\dfrac{-12}{2 \times 3}$

**OR**

attempt to complete the square ***(M1)***

$3(x - 2)^2 - 12 + p$

**OR**

attempt to differentiate and equate to $0$ ***(M1)***

$f''(x) = 6x - 12 = 0$

**THEN**

$q = 2$ ***A1***

parts.label: b
parts.intro: The vertex of the graph of $f'$ lies on the $x$-axis.
parts.text:
(i) Write down the value of the discriminant of $f'$.

(ii) Hence or otherwise, find the value of $p$.
parts.markscheme:
(i) discriminant $= 0$ ***A1***

(ii) **EITHER**

attempt to substitute into $b^2 - 4ac$ ***(M1)***

$(-12)^2 - 4 \times 3 \times p = 0$ ***A1***

**OR**

$f'(2) = 0$ ***(M1)***

$-12 + p = 0$ ***A1***

**THEN**

$p = 12$ ***A1***

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the value of the gradient of the graph of $f'$ at $x = 0$.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Sketch the graph of $f''$, the second derivative of $f$. Indicate clearly the $x$-intercept and the $y$-intercept.
parts.markscheme:
![Sketch of f″: a straight line with positive gradient through (2, 0) and (0, −12).](content/papers/img/2022-may-p1-tz1-q7d-ms.png)

***A1A1***

> **Note:** Award ***A1*** for line with positive gradient, ***A1*** for correct intercepts.

parts.label: e
parts.intro: The graph of $f$ has a point of inflexion at $x = a$.
parts.text:
(i) Write down the value of $a$.

(ii) Find the values of $x$ for which the graph of $f$ is concave-down. Justify your answer.
parts.markscheme:
(i) $a = 2$ ***A1***

(ii) $x < 2$ ***A1***

$f''(x) < 0$ (for $x < 2$) OR the $f''$ is below the $x$-axis (for $x < 2$)

OR ![Sign diagram of f″: negative for x less than 2, positive for x greater than 2.](content/papers/img/2022-may-p1-tz1-q7e-ms.png) (sign diagram must be labelled $f''$) ***R1***
